analysis.title: Goldman Sees 10Y Yields Sliding 50bps To 4.6% In 2027 As Bonds Finally Get Their Hedge Back
key_insights: Goldman's 2027 Global Rates Outlook ('A Better Buffer', William Marshall's team) sees 10Y UST yields falling from 5.13% to 4.6% by YE27, 10Y Gilts from 5.32% to 4.8%, 10Y Bunds from 3.37% to 3.1%, and 10Y JGBs flat near 2.75%.

Goldman's thesis is that markets price too much tightening almost everywhere. Its 2027 policy-rate expectations are more dovish than end-2027 market pricing in every G10 market except Japan, where it expects the BoJ to hike faster than priced.

Goldman's economists still expect two more Fed hikes before 'hawkish risks abate', with core PCE falling from 3.2% at end-2026 to 2.4% at end-2027 as tariff effects fall out and the Iran war boost to inflation fades. Cuts start only by year-end 2027.

Near-term Treasury path is 'likely to be somewhat range-bound', with returns coming mainly from interest income until the endpoint of the hiking cycle is clear. AI-related pressures are expected to keep a floor under yields in 1H27.

The rally case depends on the AI-adoption and job-market-weakness link coming into clearer view. Goldman's economists added a hike after last Tuesday's hot core CPI, so the baseline has become more hawkish even as it stays more dovish than the market.

Three sources of support for duration longs: high starting yields, a less hawkish policy path than priced, and bonds' improved hedge value. Starting yield does most of the work, and 10Y Treasuries are projected to beat T-bills in 2027 for only the second time since 2020, after another losing year in 2026.

Goldman estimates firmly positive total returns to YE27 across most of the G10, with Gilts and Treasuries at roughly 10% each (the article's read of the chart), mostly from interest income. Switzerland, with the 10Y at 0.57%, has 'little scope for capital gains'.
Valuation model: 5y5y forwards are slightly above fair value in the US, slightly below in Germany, and cheap in Japan and the UK.

Hedge value depends on inflation. When core CPI is above 2.5%, the 1-year correlation between the S&P 500 and 10Y yields averages about +30. When core is at or below 1.75% it averages about -35. With core still well above 2.5%, bonds hedge AI equity scares but not inflation scares.

Curves: Goldman expects 2s10s to steepen in the US, Germany and the UK, with the largest steepening in Gilts (budget and term premium risk) and the JGB curve flattening against the rest. In the US and Germany the preferred expression is longs in the 5Y belly.

Inflation split: the US selloff was driven by real yields, while Europe and the UK repriced inflation. Goldman favors US 10Y TIPS longs against beta-weighted shorts in 10Y nominals, and in Europe and the UK nominal longs in near-dated forwards (EUR 1y1y, 1y2y) plus inflation-curve steepeners.

US supply is better than feared. Net coupon supply (ex-bills) dips from $1.224 trillion to $1.097 trillion, with Treasury baseline lifting 2-to-10Y auction sizes from August and keeping the long end stable. Fed reserve management purchases of about $25bn/month help from 2Q27.
Germany and Japan are the supply outliers. Free float as a share of GDP rises 1-2pp in the US and UK, 4pp in Germany and 6-7pp in Japan, so Goldman expects renewed Bund cheapening versus swaps.

Debt ceiling: Goldman says it will likely bind in 1Q27. A $400bn TGA drawdown would put about 4bps of downward pressure on SOFR, but rebuilding the TGA afterward could drain liquidity with reserves near the steeper part of the demand curve, risking wider swings in funding costs, first easier then tighter.
ECB: excess liquidity of about EUR 2 trillion is above the median bank preference of about EUR 1 trillion. Goldman expects the ECB to be reactive rather than proactive on ending QT.

European spreads: energy relief should tighten high-beta names, worth about 20-30bp on 10Y BTP-Bund. France's political uncertainty is likely the most durable and may extend past the June parliamentary elections, though OATs look about 50bp cheap to fair value.

Spread forecasts: 10Y OAT-Bund at 130bp by mid-2027 and 100bp by end-2027, conditional on the next administration signaling credible deficit reduction. BTP-Bund at 105bp and 90bp, Spanish Bonos at 45bp all year.

Rates vol: implied vol is at a substantial premium to fair value after AI disruption fears and the US-Iran conflict. Goldman favors selling gamma and fading 2027 ECB hike pricing by selling EUR payers. In the US it sees downside growth scares as the more potent tail catalyst and recommends 6m-to-1y expiries on 2Y-to-5Y low-strike receivers.

The author's view is that the 4.6% target needs oil to drift lower, inflation to cooperate and fiscal discipline in Washington, Paris and Tokyo. The most likely outcome is a long range where the coupon is the return, until a growth scare delivers the rally.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman expects most of the decline in the second half of 2027, with 1H27 range-bound and carry driving returns.
Gilts are one of the two largest expected rallies, alongside USTs.
A more measured decline, held back by German fiscal expansion and heavier supply.
Rangebound, as BoJ hikes and inflation anchored around target let the curve converge to global norms.
Disinflation from tariff effects fading and the Iran war inflation boost waning is what lets the Fed stop hiking and start cutting by year-end 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Long 5Y belly in US Treasuries and German Bunds
trade_ideas.rationale: 2s5s historically moves sideways after the final hike before steepening further out, so the belly insulates against near-term policy path uncertainty without giving up much upside.

trade_ideas.description: Long 10Y TIPS against beta-weighted short 10Y nominal Treasuries
trade_ideas.rationale: Breakevens have fallen more than oil would justify, and the US selloff was driven by real yields.

trade_ideas.description: Long near-dated EUR forwards (1y1y or 1y2y) and inflation-curve steepeners in Europe and the UK
trade_ideas.rationale: Front-end inflation pricing looks rich in Europe and the UK, where the energy shock repriced inflation.

trade_ideas.description: Sell EUR payers and sell gamma
trade_ideas.rationale: Implied vol is at a substantial premium to fair value and sovereign stress acts as a speed limit on core yields, so 2027 ECB hike pricing is faded.

trade_ideas.description: Buy 6m-to-1y expiry low-strike receivers on 2Y-to-5Y rates as a growth-scare hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: Downside growth scares are now the more potent tail catalyst in the US as the upward push on implied vol from rising yields has run its course.

trade_ideas.description: Gilt 2s10s steepener (with JGB curve flattening versus other markets)
trade_ideas.rationale: The gap between the market's peak policy path and Goldman's terminal rate forecast is largest in the UK, and fiscal questions may command a stickier term premium.

risk_factors: Hot inflation prints. Goldman's economists added a Fed hike after last Tuesday's hot core CPI, and the baseline keeps getting more hawkish.
Fiscal news that reinvigorates worries about the supply/demand balance for JGBs, and fiscal slippage in Washington, Paris and Tokyo.
AI-related pressures that may keep a floor under yields in 1H27.
Stocks and bonds can fall together while core inflation stays above 2.5%, limiting bonds' hedge value against inflation scares.
Debt ceiling and TGA rebuild liquidity drain, with the risk of wider swings in funding costs than the SOFR-FF curve implies.
French political uncertainty that may extend past the June 2027 elections, with the OAT-Bund forecast conditional on credible deficit reduction.
Oil failing to drift lower while the Iran war continues.
vol_and_positioning: Rates implied vol is at a substantial premium to fair value, and Europe's rise in implied vol this year was about 70% of the 2022 increase despite smaller moves in gas prices and yields.
Goldman's baseline favors selling gamma and fading 2027 ECB hike pricing by selling EUR payers, since sovereign stress acts as a speed limit on core yields.
In the US, the upward push on implied vol from rising yields has largely run its course and downside growth scares are the more potent tail catalyst.
Recommended US hedge: 6m-to-1y expiries on 2Y-to-5Y low-strike receivers, which pay off if growth rather than inflation is the next thing to crack.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict and the Iran war energy shock pushed up implied rates vol and inflation, and Goldman's inflation path assumes the war's boost to inflation wanes.
French political uncertainty is likely to be most durable and may extend past the parliamentary elections in June 2027.
Next year's UK budget raises fiscal questions that may command a stickier term premium in Gilts.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees 10Y UST yields falling from 5.13% to 4.6% by YE27 on high starting yields, a less hawkish path than priced, and improved hedge value, with positive excess returns over T-bills in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The article argues the target needs oil to fall, inflation to cooperate and fiscal discipline everywhere, and that the likelier outcome is a long range where the coupon is the whole return. Goldman's own economists added a hike after the hot core CPI.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further hot core inflation prints that push Goldman's hike count higher, or fiscal news that renews JGB supply/demand worries.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman says recent AI-related equity volatility has uncovered duration's role as a portfolio diversifier, and lower energy prices should reinforce it.
tension_points.bear_case: With core inflation well above 2.5%, the historical S&P 500 to 10Y yield correlation is about +30, so bonds hedge AI scares but not inflation scares. Stocks and bonds fell together after Tuesday's CPI and Thursday's 30Y auction.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core inflation staying above 2.5%, where the stock-bond correlation averages about +30.

tension_points.bull_case: OATs trade about 50bp cheap to fair value and Goldman forecasts 10Y OAT-Bund at 100bp by end-2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Political uncertainty is likely to be most durable and may extend past the June parliamentary elections, and the article treats 100bp as the bull case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The next administration failing to signal credible steps towards deficit reduction.
